hook.text: In 1824, Sadi Carnot imagined a perfect engine — one with zero friction and no irreversible losses.

buildup.text: Carnot's engine runs between a hot and cold reservoir using only reversible processes. It's a thought experiment.

discovery.text: Its efficiency depends only on the temperatures. Hotter source or colder sink means higher efficiency.

twist.text: No real engine can match Carnot's ideal. But it tells engineers the absolute ceiling they can never exceed.

climax.text: A Carnot engine between 500K and 300K is 40% efficient. Real engines at those temps manage about 30%.

punchline.text: The perfect engine is impossible. But it shows us how close we can get.

quiz.question: What determines the efficiency of a Carnot engine?
options: The size of the engine and the quality of its materials
Only the temperatures of the hot source and cold sink
The type of gas used inside the engine cylinder
